findings.evidence: Hyperbolic/Volume.lean:44 `[TopologicalSpace M] [T3Space M] [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I ∞ M]`; Hyperbolic.lean:43 has the same binders for `HyperbolicMetric`; Mostow.lean:75 `[TopologicalSpace M] [T3Space M]`.
findings.fix: Replace `[MetricSpace W]` with `[TopologicalSpace W] [T3Space W]`, and likewise for `M`, in the universal statement and the `variable` block. The existential part can keep `MetricSpace` or switch the same way.
findings.issue: The universal part of `GabaiMeyerhoffMilleyTheorem` (lines 81, 84) and the `variable` block for the application lemmas (lines 105, 107) assume `[MetricSpace W]` and `[MetricSpace M]`. The statement never uses these metrics, and they are unrelated to `gW` and `g`. `HyperbolicMetric` and `hypVolumeOfMetric` only need `[TopologicalSpace M] [T3Space M]`; Lindelöf follows from compactness. Callers of the existing T3-level volume and Mostow API cannot apply the lemmas without choosing an unrelated metric.

findings.evidence: `Homeomorph` takes two types in arbitrary universes, and `hypVolumeOfMetric` returns `ℝ`. Mostow.lean:73 quantifies `{M : Type uM}` with its own universe.
findings.fix: Give them separate universes, e.g. `universe uW uM` with `W : Type uW` and `M : Type uM`, in `GabaiMeyerhoffMilleyTheorem` and in the variables of the application lemmas.
findings.issue: `W` and `M` are both `Type u` in the universal statement (lines 81, 84) and in the lemma variables (lines 105, 107). This forces them into one universe, although `hypVolumeOfMetric ≤` and `Nonempty (M ≃ₜ W)` are well-typed for types in different universes.

summary: The Gabai–Meyerhoff–Milley statement and its application lemmas require `[MetricSpace W]`/`[MetricSpace M]`, which is stronger than the `[TopologicalSpace] [T3Space]` that `HyperbolicMetric`/`hypVolumeOfMetric` need, and they force `W` and `M` into one universe. The Orientation and Weeks-definition files are at the natural level.
